author: winter oak
title: Chinese communism and the usual suspects
content:
by Paul Cudenec, who reads the article 

here




The seizure of power by the communists in 1949 led to a brutal and murderous assault on Chinese life that was even worse than that experienced by Russians under the Bolsheviks.




In January 1958 Mao Zedong, the chairman of the Chinese Communist Party (CCP), launched the regime’s second five-year plan, known as the Great Leap Forward.




Says

 

Wikipedia

: “The purpose of the plan was to use heavy industry to expedite the production of raw materials such as steel as a supplement to economic growth, similar to the Soviet model and the defining factor behind Mao’s Chinese Marxist policies.




“Mao spent ten months touring the country in 1958 to gain support for the Great Leap Forward and inspect the progress that had already been made. What this entailed was the humiliation, public castigation and torture of all who questioned the leap”. [1]




This rapid industrial “growth” and “development”, with people being sucked from the countryside into the cities, was a disaster – millions died from the resulting famine.




Author Frank Dikötter puts the death toll from 1958 to 1962 at more than 45 million Chinese – of these, around 7% were tortured and killed by the government, 2% committed suicide and 5% died in Mao’s labour camps built to hold dissidents. [2]




He describes severe punishments for slight infractions, such as being buried alive for stealing a handful of grain or losing an ear and being branded for digging up a potato.










The so-called 

Cultural Revolution

, which began in 1966, was an insanely cruel effort to impose “modernisation” and destroy all that was traditional.




Mao’s Red Guards sought to wipe out the “Four Olds” (old ideas, old culture, old customs, and old habits), often by desecrating historical artifacts and cultural and religious sites. Tens of millions of people were persecuted and sometimes massacred – up to 2 million died. [3]




I have previously explained how the 

Bolshevik

, 

Fascist

 and 

Nazi

 regimes – which likewise combined rabid industrialism with authoritarian terror – were all controlled by the entity I call ZIM, the zio-imperialist mafia. [4] But who could have been behind the nightmarish communist tyranny that subsequently took hold of China?




Yitzhak Shichor of the University of Haifa and Hebrew University of Jerusalem sheds some light on the matter in a fascinating 

paper

 published in the 

International Journal of China Studies

 in 2020.




He writes: “Jews were deeply involved in Communist revolutions in Europe, and primarily in Russia, often in leading positions. This is understandable given their demographic location, extensive education and suffering over the years.




“However, how could we account for the fact that they also played a role in Communist revolutions in Asia, and especially in China? There were practically no Jewish communities to speak of and those few who lived there had been almost totally assimilated, and had no interest whatsoever in Chinese culture, history and politics.




“Still, Jews (who arrived out of China) not only took part in the revolution but had also helped igniting it and then stayed on or joined later”. [5]










Shichor (

pictured

) says of these Jewish participants: “Their main value to the revolution was mainly writing, translation, communication and publication. Although they were all deeply committed to the Chinese Communist revolution, some of them were jailed – for years – and occasionally more than once. Nonetheless, they continued to believe in, and even to justify, the Chinese Communist Party”. [6]




Shichor explains that the Marxist brand of socialism, which reached China via Japan, was initially 

the least attractive

 to Chinese intellectuals.




“Considered too violent, the notions of ‘class struggle’ contradicted traditional Confucian values of harmonious and integrative society, and the thought that ‘workers’ represented the ‘universal’ and ‘revolutionary’ class, did not conform to pre-modern Chinese beliefs…




“Whatever socio-political opposition and ideological radicalism existed, they were articulated not by Marxist communism, but by anarchism. Mao Zedong, one of the founders and later leader of the Chinese Communist Party (CCP), regarded himself as anarchist up to the early 1920s”. [7]




But Marxism-Leninism soon came to the fore, thanks to the influence of the Bolsheviks, and Schichor reveals that “many of the chief Soviet and Comintern missionaries in China were Jewish”. [8]




He looks at the signficant role of 

Mikhail Borodin (1884-1951)

, born Mikhail Markovich Gruzenberg, saying that he is usually associated with the Nationalist Party in China (

Guomindang

, GMD), but that “his mission was ultimately and fundamentally to promote the CCP”. [9]










Borodin (

pictured

) was to adopt the usual communist approach of disassociating himself from any particular ethnic roots, but it is interesting to note that at the age of 16 he had joined the 

Bund

 (the General Jewish Workers’ Union), an organisation which placed great emphasis on Jewish identity. [10]




Adolph Abramovich Joffe (1883-1927)

, born in the Crimea to a Jewish-Karaite family and a participant in the Bolshevik revolution, was the Soviet ambassador to the official government in Beijing from 1922 to 1924 and “tried hard to convince Sun Yat-sen [the nationalist revolutionary prime minister] to trust Moscow”. [11]




Shichor writes: “While Marxism-Leninism had existed in parts of China as a 

theory

, turning it into an organized 

activity

 began with Comintern missionaries, headed by 

Grigorii Naumovitch Voitinski [1893-1953]

, who dealt with setting up the CCP… the idea of forming a CCP had already circulated by that time, but no actions had been taken, before his arrival, aged 27, in April 1920″.




Voitinski – born Grigorii Naumovitch Zarkhin to a Jewish family in Nevel, Russia – is considered by historians to have exercised “an immense influence on the Chinese Communist Movement”, he adds. [12]




“In 1920 he became deputy director of the Comintern’s Far Eastern Bureau and left for China, where he met with Chen Duxiu and Li Dazhao, the future CCP leaders.




“Although Chen toyed with the Communist idea as early as 1918, he had also been attracted by other ideas (like federalism). It was only after he met Voitinski (

pictured

) that he became committed to Communism, not just in theory but also, and more important, in practice.










“It was following his meetings with Voitinski that the first communist cells had been formed – at least seven in different cities and provinces, before the CCP was organized. Voitinski’s promotion of Marxist study groups not only paved the ground for the establishment of Party cells but also for distributing Marxist-Leninist knowledge that Chinese intellectuals had been lacking”. [13]




“His impact was felt not only in the emergence of anti-US feelings among Chinese intellectuals, but also, and more significantly, in fighting anarchism and in its eventual demise”. [14]




A key role of industrialist and authoritarian communism has always been to crush all real opposition to the empire of greed whose agenda it secretly serves.




As an aside, some insights into Chinese anarchism can be found in an 

essay

 by Robert Scalpino and George T. Yu.




They argue: “Anarchism, whatever its utopian qualities for modern China, was in many respects also naturally Chinese. It was the other side of the Confucian, educative, centralized, authoritarian state. It was the scholar in contemplation and out of office, the peasant out of reach of his landlord, the wanderer beyond the outstretched hands of the state. Indeed, it was the imperishable goal of all men at all times – complete freedom for self realization within the limits of social justice, to the limits of one’s capacity”. [15]










They cite a definition of anarchism that appeared in the movement’s journal 

Hsin Shih chi

 (‘The New Century’) in 1907: “The individual is the basic unit in society. Together with others, he forms a village, and with other villages, a country is formed. Society in turn is formed through the process of bringing all countries together.




“The proper society is that which permits free exchange between and among individuals, mutual aid, the common happiness and enjoyment of all, and the freedom from control by the force of a few. This is what Anarchism seeks to realize.




“The governments of today, however, are organized by the few, who in turn pass laws which are of benefit to the few. Thus the state is the destroyer of the proper society. In sum, what we seek is the destruction of the destroyer of proper society”. [16]




It is quite clear why those out to destroy “proper society” in favour of global “communist” tyranny would want to wipe out the alternative presented by anarchism.




The authors note: “Historically, Marxism was unable to make inroads into China until after the Russian Revolution of 1917 when Lenin’s followers, bankrolled by the Bolshevik government, began their attacks on Anarchists in Russia and neighboring countries…




“There is no better way to see the authoritarian elements in Communist theory than to read the Communist polemics directed against the Anarchist”.










To this effect, they quote the aforementioned Chen (

pictured

), the leading spokesman for the Chinese communists. He described the Chinese people as corrupt and backward and said that, if they were to be saved, there had to be “strict interference” in economic and political matters, an “enlightened despotism”. The chief obstacle to this was the “lazy, wanton, illegal sort of free thought that forms a part of our people’s character”. [17]




Although, from my perspective, many Chinese anarchists at the time were worryingly enthusiastic about “progress” and “science”, Scalpino and Yu add: “Ch’en pursued another theme with vigor: Anarchism would have man return to primitivism. Economically, it would take him back to the era of handicraft industries. Politically, it would remove him to the days of tribalism”. [18]




Chinese revolutionaries were taken to the USSR to undergo Bolshevik brainwashing: in 1925, a first wave of some 340 Chinese students – both GMD and CCP – arrived in Moscow to attend the new Sun Yat-sen University.




The first rector of this institution was 

Karl Radek (1885-1939)

, 

pictured

, who was born Karol Sobelsohn to a Jewish family in Lvov, Ukraine.










Shichor comments: “As the rector of Sun Yat-sen University, he must have influenced Chinese students – both left and right… One of his sentences, published in 1925 and related to the prospects of the CCP to seize power, could be regarded, in retrospect, as a prediction: in the course of its revolutionary struggles, the Chinese proletariat, together with the petty bourgeoisie, ‘will be forced for the time being to develop the economic power of the land in a capitalist fashion'”. [19]




Among the Jewish activists who associated themselves with Chinese communism were a number of Americans, we learn.




One of these was 

Sidney Rittenberg (1921-2019)

: “Influenced by his grandfather (on his mother’s side), who had been a Russian Jewish revolutionary, Rittenberg joined the American Communist Party in 1940 when he was eighteen”. [20]




“When he arrived in China in September 1945, the war was over… Usually, Chinese he met did not know what a Jew was. He began to meet Chinese communists and, as a soldier free to move, did them modest favours – including helping several underground activists to escape from the police”. [21]




“Sometime by late 1946 or early 1947, Rittenberg became a Party member, approved by the top communist leaders, including Mao, Liu Shaoqi, Zhou Enlai, Ren Bishi and Zhu De. He was the first US citizen to become a CCP member. His main role was to make information about communist victories – discounted and ignored outside China – available to the West”. [22]










Shichor relates that for a few months in 1967, Rittenberg (

pictured

) was the head of China’s Broadcast Administration (Radio Beijing), at a time “when the Cultural Revolution was turning nasty”.




His activity there apparently led to certain “antisemitic” critics complaining that “Rittenberg shows all the qualities we have long been accustomed to finding in the Jew”. [23]




Shichor relates that after his return to the USA, Rittenberg continued his mission – to “make China more accessible to the West” – but now spurning revolutionary talk for an economic message. [24]




Rittenberg was, it seems, interviewed on CBS network’s 

60 Minutes

 more than any other individual and, in parallel, he founded a consulting firm for American companies doing business in China.




Says Shichor: “He offered his services, personal connections and familiarity with the Chinese system, turning into a full-fledge capitalist, making millions of dollars. As such, he personally embodied the combination post-Mao China has been attempting, a socialist market economy, capitalism under a communist system. This unprecedented innovation was introduced to China mainly by Jewish economists”. [25]




More on that shortly.




Another key Jewish figure in Chinese communism was 

Israel Epstein (1915-2005)

, 

pictured

, whose worldview Shichor describes as “a combination of orthodox Judaism and European enlightened modernism”. [26]










He became a naturalized Chinese citizen and was one of the founders of a pro-industry magazine called 

China Reconstructs

, taking on the role of editor-in-chief in 1979.




Shichor adds: “In 1983, he was admitted to the CPPCC (Chinese People’s Political Consultative Conference). Half of its ten non-Chinese members at one time were Jewish. Jews played constructive roles in most of China’s media, directed to the outside world”. [27]




Yet another of these propagandists was 

Sidney Shapiro (1915-2014)

, who was born to a Jewish family in Brooklyn, New York.




“After graduating, he joined a prominent firm of Jewish Wall Street lawyers. He left New York in March 1947, not for any ideological motives or communist inclinations, but hoping to improve his Chinese while seeking a job as a business lawyer for an American firm in Beijing. Through his would-be Chinese wife, he approached the communists…




“Soon employed by the Bureau of Cultural Relations with Foreign Countries, Shapiro became a translator of books and pamphlets. He still insisted that he ‘wasn’t much of a Marxist’”. [28]










“In the early 1960s, Shapiro (

pictured

) finally decided that he had the kind of life he wanted most. He realized he ‘could do more useful and satisfying work in Peking than in New York’, and in 1963 applied for Chinese citizenship, which he received a few months later”. [29]




David Crook (1910-2000)

 was born in London, England, to a Jewish family of Eastern European origins.




He joined the Communist Party in 1936, went off to be part of the International Brigades in the Spanish Civil War and was promptly “recruited by the KGB”. Shichor reveals: “He began spying on leftist ‘elements’ who opposed the Soviet Union, and especially Stalin… In May 1938, on Soviet orders, he left for Shanghai… Officially, he was teaching literature at St. John’s University and later at Suzhou University. Unofficially he spied, especially on ‘Trotskyists'”. [30]




During the Second World War Crook (

pictured below

) joined the RAF and became an officer but was demoted because he was “suspected of spying for the Soviets” – correctly so, presumably! [31]




After the war he went to live in China and by the early 1950s had become deputy dean in the English Department of what was to become the Beijing Foreign Languages Institute.




Shichor explains: “Crook’s teaching concentrated on training interpreters and translators who would escort foreign visitors, rather than ‘wasting’ time on teaching literature he considered ‘impractical’ at best, and ‘intellectual’ at worst. Many of his thousands of students ‘reached the highest ranks in the foreign ministry and in academia'”. [32]










Crook’s propagandistic activities in the 1970s included a three-month-tour in the world outside the communist state “where he spoke in favour of the Cultural Revolution and China”. [33]




A second “British Jew who became full-fledged pro-Chinese spokesman”, as Shichor puts it, was 

Michael Shapiro (1910-1986)

.




I 

see

 that he was actually born in Ukraine, but his family settled in the East End of London and he gained British nationality in 1931. He joined the Young Communist League in 1931 and the Communist Party of Great Britain in 1934. [34]




Shichor says: “In 1949, or 1950, he left for China, reportedly ‘at the invitation of the Chinese Communist Party Central Committee, and on the assignment of the British Communist Party’ and was attached to the China Information Bureau”. [35]




“Michael Shapiro (

pictured

) never returned to the UK. Until his death in 1986, a total of 36 years, he worked at Xinhua News Agency and Foreign Languages Press, copy-editing English commentaries for the Department of Home News for Overseas Service, as well as translating the works of Mao Zedong and Liu Shaoqi. This was the Western ‘foreign experts” – many of them Jewish – main mission, as demonstrated in the following episode.










“In late 1959, the CCP Central Committee decided to form a team to translate a fourth volume of Mao’s 

Selected Works

 into English, and to revise the outdated English translation of the first three volumes, issued by the mid-1950s.




“Work began in early 1960 by a team of fourteen, of which nine were Chinese (Oxford-educated scholars, Foreign Ministry, Foreign Languages Press and Foreign Languages Institute officials) and five foreigners: Sydney Rittenberg, Frank Coe, Israel Epstein, Sol Adler, and Michael Shapiro – all Jewish”. [36]




But Jewish influence on communist China was not merely cultural, as Shichor proudly relates.







In the late 1970s, as soon as Beijing’s post-Mao leaders decided it was time to undertake wide-ranging economic reform (which some had in mind since the early 1950s), discussions were held with leading foreign economic experts, invited to China. Intentionally, or not, most of them were Jewish. Historically, Jews were usually associated with money (capital), for better or for worse. Skilled in commerce and banking, educated, urban yet highly mobile, and with worldwide family connections – Jews represented modernity, and a most significant driving force behind capitalist growth and development. Marx himself specifically equated capitalism with Judaism. Jews also excelled in research: 40 percent of all Nobel Prize winners in economics and 51 percent of all US economics Nobel Prize winners were Jewish. Some of them helped China to become the second – perhaps the leading – world economic power. [37]







The Jewish “experts” invited to red China in 1979 included the economist 

Milton Friedman (1912-2006)

, who accepted and made the trip. [38]




Shichor adds: “Another delegation visited China in 1979. Headed by the University of Pennsylvania Profesor Lawrence Klein (who won the 1980 economics Nobel Prize), it included professor Irma Adelman, [of] the Department of Agricultural and Resource Economics, the Graduate School of the University of California, Berkeley; and Kenneth Arrow of Harvard University (who had won the Nobel Prize in 1972) – all Jewish”. [39]










Then in November 1988 Chinese prime minister Zhao Ziyang met and sought advice from the American-Israeli 

Stanley Fischer (1943-2025)

, who had earlier that year become chief economist of the World Bank. [40]




Fischer 

went on

 to be deputy managing director of the International Monetary Fund, governor of the Bank of Israel and vice chair of the US Federal Reserve. Oh, and he was also an executive at Citigroup, a senior advisor at BlackRock, a “Distinguished Fellow” of the Council on Foreign Relations and a member of the Bilderberg Group. [41]




Are there really still people out there who think that all these global inter-connections are coincidental and that to suggest otherwise is to spread “anti-semitic conspiracy theories”?

author: dev
title: Octobre 26 n'a pas encore eu lieu
content:
Plusieurs membres du Groupe Fernand Illich ont recueilli des témoignages de lycéens depuis début novembre 26, et témoigné eux-mêmes de ce qu'ils ont pu voir dans les lycées et dans les manifestations qui se poursuivent en ce moment. Ces témoignages sont ici montés en alternance, avec des flashbacks d'octobre 26 et des flashforwards spéculatifs d'un avenir possible pour l'école. Toutes ces images composent ensemble un film dont le message est clair : Octobre 26 n'a pas encore eu lieu, Octobre 26 est encore à venir.




 

12 novembre 26, 8h.

 

 Les élèves arrivent au compte-goutte en classe. C'est à cause de 

la fouille

, madame. La fouille ? Oui, à la grille. Maintenant, ils nous fouillent et ça crée des queues monstres : on attend qu'ils aient contrôlé nos sacs pour pouvoir rentrer. Qui ça, « ils » ? Les élèves ne savent pas très bien dire. Des vigiles. Des surveillants, la vie scolaire. Le CPE. Ça se mélange. Tous ceux qui participent à la fouille sont qualifiés ensemble par un même pronom à valeur indéfinie et pourtant parfaitement clair pour les élèves : « ils ». Trois vigiles, en effet, ont été employés depuis les alertes incendie déclenchées en série à la rentrée. Octobre 26 avait mis le feu aux poubelles devant les grilles des lycées. Avec la répression, le feu ne s'est pas éteint, il est entré dans les murs : départs de feu sporadiques dans les toilettes (des élèves brûlent le papier toilette), plusieurs fois par jour. C'est un nouveau pattern d'action : le feu dans les lycées. ILS ont désactivé les alarmes incendie, dit un élève, sinon on serait tout le temps en train d'évacuer. Mais c'est dangereux, ça, non ? C'est illégal, non, madame ? ILS tournent toute la journée. De toute façon, maintenant, les toilettes sont toutes fermées sauf une. Il y a des queues monstres devant. Les vigiles sont là pour rassurer. (Comme les flics qui nous prothèsent.) Trois vigiles spécialisés dans l'évacuation des bâtiments, paraît-il. Habillés en tenue de sécurité. Racisés. Sous-payés. Exploités pour contribuer à casser un mouvement qui se bat dans leur propre intérêt objectif. Assignés aux opérations de contrôle.




Et la police ? Il y a une voiture devant l'établissement, presque tous les matins. Gyrophare. Des arrestations musclées et ciblées ont eu lieu à la rentrée, lundi 2, mardi 3. Un élève jeté au sol et matraqué a eu un bras cassé. Ils ont ciblé les plus actifs du mouvement. Un prof dit : J'ai plusieurs élèves arrêtés, sur Pronote c'est marqué dans la liste, devant leur nom, « mesure conservatoire ». En attente d'une exclusion. Maintenant que les plus actifs sont arrêtés, la fouille et le contrôle peuvent se faire sans la police. Voilà l'un des effets contre-révolutionnaires d'octobre 26 : des alliances circonstancielles ont été nouées entre le milieu scolaire et les forces de l'ordre, par lesquelles la fonction policière a été détachée de la police, pour être un peu répartie entre administratifs, surveillants, vigiles privés. On dit « ils » pour désigner cette fonction abstraite, devenue liquide, qui circule entre les mains, entre les yeux. Le lycée est sous occupation policière, 

sans même que ce soit la seule police qui l'occupe

, car la police s'est instillée et diffusée dans les pratiques et dans le rapport structurel aux élèves. Le CPE n'est pas content du tout du mouvement lycéen, il ne comprend pas ce qui se passe, il dit : Mais ils peuvent s'exprimer ! Il y a le Conseil de Vie Lycéenne pour ça, il y a les instances, il y a déjà tout ce qu'il faut ! Il est présent à la grille dès 7h30 le matin. Conseiller Principal d'Épuration. Les poubelles sont surveillées. Déplacées. Mises en sûreté. L'école-caserne réagit à sa propre crise en sortant ses épines comme un hérisson et comme un virus.




« Plus jamais ça », avait dit Macron, « plus jamais le 17 octobre ». En disant ces mots avec pompe solennité, il réactive d'instinct l'imaginaire français de la guerre, de la « der des ders » (comme il l'avait déjà fait, du reste, dans des occasions à chaque fois diminuées et ridicules, en déclarant le confinement de 2020 : « nous sommes en guerre », ou comme il l'avait encore fait après sa Grande Dissolution en juin 24, en parlant ensuite du danger de « guerre civile »). « Plus jamais le 17 », traduction : 

guerre aux pauvres !

 Passons ce genre d'énoncés illico au traducteur. Traduction : « Laissez l'État gérer la répression sans limite, sinon vous devrez vous protéger vous-même comme des 

vigilantes

 », bouchers-charcutiers avec vos gros hachoirs, coiffeuses avec vos petits ciseaux, bijoutiers avec vos chaînes en or, vous devrez faire fuir les pillards à coups de lacrymo de poche (lacrymo portable pour dame, pour boubta fragile). La fiction de 

l'État nécessaire

 ne tient plus qu'à quelques cheveux.


Traduction : L'ÉTAT NASSE ET SERRE.


(Images en flashbacks du 31 octobre, à Toulouse, Marseille, Bordeaux ou Lyon : on a cru parfois voir une manifestation de flics carapacés pour la nuit d'Halloween, tant ils grouillaient, attendant les manifestants « venus pour en découdre ». 

« 1 prof pour 36 élèves, 6 flics par lycéen.ne mobilisé.e ! »

 Vision de police-apocalypse : on imagine bientôt dans les villes des grandes places désertes comme pendant le covid, balayées par des nuées de gaz blanc. Ces images s'enchaînent avec celles d'aujourd'hui : la police est passée en nous, gazéifiée elle aussi, molécularisée ; elle a infiltré l'école, a pénétré les yeux des gentils surveillants-étudiants sous-payés qui font ouvrir les sacs à la grille en disant bonne journée.)




La même chose se passe à l'école en ce moment : « plus jamais ça », plus jamais la volte-face de ceux que l'école exclut de la réussite. Laissez-vous faire, lumpen-étudiants. Vous n'en avez pas eu assez avec vos mauvaises notes, vos mauvaises orientations, vos refus à Parcoursup ? Alors vous aurez les menottes et les bras cassés.


Et ils ne vous touchent pas au moins, pendant la Fouille ? Ne vous laissez pas toucher. (Un collègue dit qu'il faudra peut-être faire des cours d'anti-rep à la rentrée dès la Seconde.) Ça dépend, répond une élève. Le plus souvent ils font juste ouvrir le sac, mais certains sont traités à part, sur le côté. Ils cherchent des mortiers cachés dans les chaussettes, dans les pantalons. Des déo, des bombes aérosols. C'est surtout ça qu'ils cherchent comme matériel politique. (Depuis octobre 26, on n'arrête pas de dire « ils ». Pronom indéfini, mais pas indéterminé : « ils » désigne une fonction à la fois impersonnelle et distincte, une idée 

distincte-obscure

.) Qu'est-ce que vous avez appris pendant ce mois d'octobre ? Est-ce que ça vous a changé.e.s ? Oui, répond l'un : Ça a radicalisé politiquement des gens très jeunes. On ne peut plus être au centre, impossible, on est rejeté par une force centrifuge. Octobre 26 a tracé une ligne autour de laquelle on est forcé de se situer. Maintenant, on est soit de droite, soit de gauche. Le marqueur, c'est le blocus. Pour ou contre. On est forcé de choisir son camp, qu'on le veuille ou non. Une autre élève réplique : Moi, je suis pour le mouvement, mais je ne bloque pas, je ne peux pas, je pense que chacun a une position plus nuancée, plus ambiguë que ce partage binaire. Tu es centriste, lui répond l'autre : Vote pour Teddy Riner ! On rigole. Et vous, madame ?




 

13 novembre 26.

 

 Les personnels « complices » des blocus auront des sanctions judiciaires ou disciplinaires, a dit le ministre. Mais maintenant que ça a rouvert, beaucoup de profs sont dans les salles comme des pigeons dans des casiers, sans voir ce qui se passe à la grille (matraque, bras cassé, menottes, fouille). S'hurle tes reins. Il y en a beaucoup, parmi les profs, qui foncent à fond dans leur programme, comme s'il ne s'était rien passé depuis fin septembre : ils veulent « rattraper le retard ». Rendez-vous compte, la fin du trimestre approche et on n'a pas de notes. Ils font tout comme avant. Les élèves ont depuis l'enfance pris l'habitude d'être gouvernés, on ne les laissera pas se gouverner eux-mêmes, même un peu. Reste assis. Attends. Écoute. Tais-toi. Lève la main. Attends encore. Et vous avez parlé du mouvement lycéen avec vos profs ? Non, enfin très peu, genre « j'espère que vous allez bien », voilà, avec un air triste et compatissant, comme si on subissait le mouvement, comme si c'était pas nous qui l'avions fait, comme si on était des passifs, des victimes du mouvement.




Pendant la semaine de distanciel on n'a jamais eu autant de travail, c'était impossible à suivre. La plupart des profs exigeaient qu'on leur rende le travail sur le créneau où on était censés avoir cours. Avec les visios, on étouffait. On a tout fait à l'IA, enfin une grande partie, c'était inévitable étant donné le rythme, on se sentait trop à la chaîne.




Pour une nouvelle économie libidinale de l'école




L'IA a fait buguer l'école. Le rôle tactique de l'IA dans le rapport de la jeunesse à la machine scolaire est l'une des choses les plus mal comprises. aura

tisation des structures de pouvoir.




Je repense aux élèves qui, chaque année, au moment du carnaval du lycée, me demandent : Monsieur, vous n'êtes pas déguisé ? Je leur réponds toujours pareil : Je suis déjà déguisé toute l'année, moi. En quoi, monsieur ? En prof, voyons. Pendant le mouvement lycéen, les déguisements ont instauré une sorte de battle d'aura face à la police. Masque contre casque, déguisement contre déguisement. C'est la fiction de l'État qui a été démasquée par ce jeu que la jeunesse a su lui imposer avec une légèreté puissante.




Pour justifier les mesures de sécurité exceptionnelles du 31 (interdiction des masques, dérogation d'exception à la dérogation légale sur les fêtes traditionnelles), le ministre Nuñez a invoqué le caractère 

terrifiant

 des appels à la manifestation du 31 diffusés sur TikTok et autres réseaux : des appels à « la nuit des ténèbres », à « l'enfer », à « la Purge ». Ouh ! ouh ! American Nightmare ! C'est horrible, ma pauvre dame, vous ne pouvez pas savoir. En communiquant de cette manière, Nuñez sait très bien à qui il parle : 

aux vieux

 

 !

, c'est-à-dire à tout ce qui, dans la société française des croûtons et croulants mentaux, peut nourrir incompréhension et ressentiment contre la jeunesse et contre sa culture. Halloween, tout ce qui vient des États-Unis, les images violentes, Netflix, les jeux vidéo, le rap, tout ça. Attention, des jeunes pourraient venir frapper à votre porte. Des jeunes : des Noirs en noir. Rendez-vous compte, ma bonne dame, « la Purge » ! C'est en effet à cette esthétique de cinéma d'horreur qu'ont puisé de nombreuses affiches pour les rassemblements du 31.







 










 










Dans la série de films dystopiques qui commence en 2013 avec 

The Purge

 (

American Nightmare

, en français), un parti nationaliste nommé « les Nouveaux Pères Fondateurs de l'Amérique » a profité de la crise économique et de la hausse de la criminalité pour parvenir au pouvoir. Sa mesure phare : l'instauration de la Purge. Une nuit par an, pendant 12 heures, s'exerce le « droit de purge ». Dans cette parenthèse, plus aucune violence n'est illégale, et même le meurtre se trouve décriminalisé. N'appelez pas la police, les pompiers, l'ambulance : personne ne viendra. Barricadez-vous. Cette mesure repose sur un postulat naturaliste : la violence serait présente dans la nature humaine comme une pulsion qui cherche à se défouler ; en donnant un exutoire légal à cette pulsion d'agression une fois par an, on pourrait la purger, l'éradiquer pour les 364 jours restants de l'année. Grâce à la Purge, la criminalité est tombée en-dessous de 1%. (Comme si la violence n'était pas un fait social, relatif à des circonstances, à des inégalités, à des rapports établis de pouvoir.)




Mais le film 

déconstruit

 justement ce postulat naturaliste. Dans les faits, ce sont les pauvres, les sans-abris, les racisés, qui sont les victimes émissaires directes de la Purge. Et ce sont les nantis blancs qui, dans une sorte de darwinisme social spontané et de normalisation du Ku Klux Klan, se masquent la nuit pour venir lyncher euphoriquement les « parasites », en toute légalité. La Purge, c'est la guerre déclarée de la société aux pauvres et aux exclus. (On ne fait pas baisser la criminalité, on persécute et massacre les pauvres qui sont contraints à la criminalité.) Le film moque la manière dont la violence envers les boucs-émissaires de la société se trouve dissimulée sous le rite sacré de « la Purge », auquel nombre de citoyens adhèrent comme à une liturgie qu'ils pratiquent ou regardent religieusement à la télé, barricadés chez eux.




Or, l'appel du 31 octobre repose précisément sur un 

renversement

 de cet imaginaire dystopique. Car ici, dans l'imaginaire de ces affiches, qu'est-ce qui est visé par « la Purge » ? Ce sont les richesses des nantis et les artifices légaux qui les protègent. Retour de bâton. Par une ironie, le personnage principal du premier film de la série (Ethan Hawke) a fait fortune grâce à la Purge, en vendant des systèmes de sécurité hi-tech pour verrouiller les maisons pendant la nuit fatidique. Ainsi le film déconstruit-il la Purge : la violence sera toujours bénie par le capitalisme, rebaptisée de prête-noms qui la dissimulent (« droit de Purge »), protégée par des dispositifs légaux, dès lors qu'elle est utile aux possédants. C'est seulement quand le rapport de domination est renversé, quand la misère sort de son ghetto pour oser porter atteinte aux biens des braves possédants, qu'elle est nommée et dénoncée comme « violence », jugée inacceptable et terrifiante.




Mais cette terreur est aussi un contre-effet positif. La lutte se joue en partie dans l'imaginaire. Ainsi y a-t-il eu une petite sorcellerie des affiches du 31, une action à distance de l'imaginaire dans le réel. À la technique de détournement de la loi, s'ajoute en effet une technique spectrale d'

iconomorphose

 : la fiction sort de sa diégèse. Elle est sur le point de transgresser la frontière qui la séparait du réel, et le réel, symétriquement, est sur le point de se métamorphoser sous son influence pénétrante, de 

se faire à l'image de la fiction

. Voilà ce qui terrifie : c'est que, soudain, 

la fiction refuse de se tenir à sa place, à l'écran

. Qu'elle refuse de nous river tous à nos écrans comme des geush fonscars d'images, comme de bons consommateurs frustrés. Soudain, la dystopie politique est dans la rue, pour une nuit. Bien sûr, la contre-Purge reste une fiction. Mais les images ne sont pas seulement des habillages décoratifs et festifs : la fiction a une efficace politique. Car grâce à cette habile terreur iconomorphique nocturne, l'État s'est trouvé forcé par l'imaginaire à s'exposer et à dévoiler son jeu dans la réalité la plus crue, à interdire par exception, c'est-à-dire à révéler encore un peu plus au grand jour son régime général d'exception. Les jeunes, qu'on accuse d'être accros à leur téléphone, aux réseaux sociaux, déréalisés par les images, ce sont eux qui nous montrent au contraire comment 

ouvrir une fenêtre

 fictionnelle dans le réel, comment déstabiliser le principe-de-réalité sacré par la force de l'imaginaire. L'école devra, elle aussi, savoir ouvrir des fenêtres.




La nuit tombe, tout devient clair.




Groupe Fernand Illich

author: none
title: Just Released: Video Taken by ALF As They Liberate 9 Mice from University of New Orleans Vivisector Christopher Harshaw
content:
On September 19, 2026, nine female mice (including four so-called “breeding females”) were loaded up and spirited away from a miserable, windowless cinderblock room on the 2nd floor of UNO’s Psychology Building to begin a new life in safety and comfort. Today for the first time, video taken by the Animal Liberation Front(ALF) during the raid is being released, after it was received anonymously and exclusively by the North American Animal Liberation Press Office.

The ALF communique received after the raid can be viewed here. The raw video footage can be viewed in its entirety here. Images in this press release are stills from the footage, are anti-copyrighted and can be used without permission.

The lab was that of Christopher Harshaw, who subjects mice and rats to experiments that purportedly aim to study autism, body temperature regulation and social behavior. This involves injecting them with drugs (such as acetaminophen to induce neurodevelopmental disorders), shutting them into small lighted cabinets overnight, and putting poisonous chemicals into their water like aniline (known to cause blood disorders and spleen tumors in rodents).

Moreover, Christopher Harshaw and his research assistant Anna are personally responsible for the killing of hundreds of animals per year, sometimes as many as 30-50 in a single day, as noted in Harwshaw’s “Euthanasia Log” notebook, which on a previous visit was removed, had its pages photocopied (along with other documents related to animal research) and then put back. His death tally: 323 in 2023 (rats and mice), 575 in 2024 (rats and mice, including one wild mouse caught in a live trap and killed on the premises), and 363 in 2025 (all mice). His method: gassing them to death with co2.

Per the communique: “To Chris Harshaw: Accessing your lab was child’s play, and with the hammer and drill on sight it would have been only too easy to decommission every piece of equipment you own. Consider this a warning. In the end you were shown more mercy than the animals you hold captive.”

For additional information, visit www.animalliberationpressoffice.org

author: Kodao Productions
title: ‘Savage Sunday’ arrests biggest in Philippine history
content:
With at least 276 protesters currently detained at Camp Bagong Diwa (CBD) in Taguig City and eight others arrested in Liwasang Bonifacio in Manila, the Ferdinand Marcos Jr. government on Sunday has committed the biggest mass arrest in the country’s history on Sunday.




Surpassing the record 244 mass arrested in the anti-corruption and anti-martial law protests in September 21, 2025, yesterday’s savage apprehensions reportedly also came with beatings of protesters under police custody.




“[S]everal other delegates remain unaccounted for, with reports that they were taken to other locations. Their exact number and whereabouts are still being verified,” the group Lakbayan ng Timog Katagalugan reported on Sunday night.




The hundreds apprehended at Sucat People’s Park in Muntinlupa City on Saturday afternoon were taken to CBD, headquarters of the National Capital Region Police Office (NCRPO) while those arrested at Liwasang Bonifacio were taken to undisclosed precincts around Manila.




The savagery included the spraying of human feces and urine before the statue of national hero Andres Bonifacio, a sacred spot for the Filipino working class, by suspected government agents to prevent protesters from erecting a protest camp.




The arrests came as Marcos Jr. opened the 49th Association of South East Asian Nations Summit and anticipating the arrival of US President Donald Trump on Tuesday.




CHR, lawyers, doctors denied access




Volunteer lawyers, paralegals, and medical professionals, as well as the Commission on Human Rights were denied access to the detainees for hours, until finally allowed access before midnight last night.




It was the first time the injured were given medical attention and food since their arrest at about 2:30 PM.




Atty. Abigail Joy Aman, one of the volunteer lawyers at the scene, said they have been requesting access to the detainees at CBD since 5PM but were refused by the police who insisted government lawyers were already “processing” the arrestees.




“We kept telling them that the detainees have the right to be represented by lawyers of their choice. [And when we were finally allowed inside], they were those who told us they were punched in the gut,” Aman told reporters.




Aman added the detainees were not committing any crime at the time of the arrest.




Lakbayan confirmed their delegates were manhandled by the police, several sustaining injuries, bruises, and complain of difficulty in walking.




“Their detention conditions are equally alarming. They are being held in an extremely hot, poorly ventilated facility with inadequate water supply, endangering their health and well-being,” the group said in a statement.




The Lakbayan originally planned to march to Liwasang Bonifacio but were delayed by blockades in Binan, Laguna on Friday and were forced to spend the night at Sucat. While resting for the night, the Southern Police District cordoned the area and subsequently mass arrested the anti-Donald Trump protesters.




Scores of journalists arrested




Two Southern Tagalog Exposure reporters, one Altermidya Network correspondent, three College Editors Guild of the Philippines coordinators, and 12 student journalists were likewise arrested in Muntinlupa on Sunday. Several suffered injuries from the brutal arrests.




The University of the Philippines-Los Banos (UPLB) Office of the Vice Chancellor for Student Affairs (OVCSA) condemned the mass arrest of their students and other participants. Nine of the arrestees from staff members of UPLB Perspective, the school’s official student publication.




“The right to peaceful assembly, freedom of expression, and collective action is guaranteed under the Philippine Constitution. Students and citizens must be able to express dissent, raise legitimate grievances, and participate in democratic processes without fear of intimidation, arbitrary arrest, or repression,” OVCSA said.




A lawyer from the Presidential Task Force on Media Security tried to negotiate their release from police custody but had been unsuccessful so far.




At Liwasang Bonifacio, two Tinig ng Plaridel (TNP, student publication of the UP College of Media and Communication) reporters narrowly escaped arrest by the police, an incident condemned by Dean Diosa Labiste.




The two student journalists were documenting manhandling of a protester when verbally abused by Manila Police District officers who attempted to arrest them. Once of the staffers suffered minor abrasions, the publication said.




“We demand that the police refrain from hampering the work of and intimidating student journalists reporting on the protest actions in the exercise of their role as campus journalists. We also demand that authorities recognize citizens’ constitutional right to participate in protest activities and report on them,” Labiste and TNP said in a statement.




‘Condemnable brutality’




Rights group Karapatan strongly condemned the mass arrests of the anti-Trump and Pax Silica activists and the journalists.




“These disturbing scenes, recorded in full public view, expose the brutality of the police and the extent to which state forces are willing to go to suppress dissent,” Karapatan said.




The group added the PNP has turned a public space meant for the exercise of people’s democratic rights into a site of violence and repression, demanding the immediate release of the detainees and a stop to physical and psychological abuse against them.




Bagong Alyansang Makabayan likewise condemned “Marcosian tactics” employed against Pax Silica protesters. “Marcos Jr. is relying on the examples set by his notorious role models: the Imeldific “clearing operations” from his mother and the repressive measures from the fascist playbook of his dictator father,” Bayan secretary general Raymond Palatino said. # 

(Raymund B. Villanueva)

‘Savage Sunday’ arrests biggest in Philippine history

author: Isaac Nellist
title: Protesters condemn state government attacks on Palestine solidarity, free speech
content:
Rallies were held across the country on November 15 to express solidarity with the people of Palestine and oppose repression of speech and protest by all levels of government.

The national day of action against repressive laws was called by Justice for Palestine Magan-djin (JFP) as part of its campaign to repeal the Queensland Liberal National Party government’s laws which criminalise Palestine solidarity slogans including “From the river to the sea” and “Globalise the intifada [uprising]”.

Chris Minns’ NSW Labor government is supporting the Queensland LNP government in the High Court challenge brought by JFP to overturn the laws. Victorian Liberals leader Jess Wilson has vowed to ban the phrase “Globalise the intifada” if elected on November 28.

JFP spokesperson Remah Naji said repression is “uniting our political class” and “thousands of us are united in defending our right to protest genocide”.

“The crimes remain the crime of genocide, the crime of occupation and the crime of apartheid. There is no amount of repression that will distract us from Israel’s crimes or absolve our government from its complicity in them.”

Michael Bradley, from MARQUE Lawyers, which is representing JFP in the High Court Case, said: “Queensland is currently leading the way with its ridiculous law that criminalises mere words, but other states are watching and keen to follow suit.

“It is more critical than ever that a stand is taken — in the courts and on the street — to demand our basic rights: to assemble, to protest and to speak.”

The crack down comes as Israel continues to kill Palestinians in Gaza and the Occupied West Bank, despite the so-called ceasefire. Its strike on the Nasser Hospital on November 12 — the only functioning hospital in Gaza — which killed six people, including surgeon Dr Rizq Shaira and a teenage patient, was condemned by 18 countries for violating international law.

As winter floods, storms and cold descend, many are still left sheltering in tents because of Israel’s restriction of supplies into Gaza. A nine-month-old baby died from hypothermia in Khan Younis in Southern Gaza on November 12 due to exposure to extreme cold.

Israel has killed at least 1610 Palestinians since the so-called ceasefire took effect.

Jonathan Strauss reports that 500 people marched in Magan-djin/Brisbane behind a large banner featuring the banned slogan “From the river to the sea”, a frequent chant of the Palestine solidarity movement.

The other banned slogan, “Globalise the intifada”, was not commonly used at Palestine rallies in Magan-djin, but expresses a desire for international support for the Palestinian people.

Anti-Zionist Jewish activist Stephen Heydt told the crowd that “kifah” means “fight” in Arabic. At the end of his speech he and others revealed t-shirts with the “globalise” slogan.

Police soon forcefully intervened, arresting seven people throughout the rally, including Heydt and two women who had carried the lead banner.

Naji said genocide was the real crime, not protesting the complicty of the Queensland and federal government.

The seven arrests add to the 31 previously made under the anti-free speech laws. Some, like Heydt, have now been arrested twice.

JFP is pursuing a High Court challenge to strike down the anti-free speech laws. It is asking for financial support for this and is organising a fundraising event on December 11.

The rally also featured music from a local punk band and a Riff Raff brass contingent.

Pip Hinman reports from Gadigal Country/Sydney that hundreds took to the streets again for Gaza on November 15. They demanded that NSW and federal Labor take action for Palestine, and stop trying to suppress free speech — particularly those speaking up against genocide.

The protest was called to show solidarity with pro-Palestine supporters in Queensland, who are being criminalised for standing up against genocide, and called for the scrapping of bans on phrases which call for rights, dignity, peace and justice for those living between the Jordan River and the Mediterranean Sea.

Minns wants to bring in similar laws, but is waiting on the outcome of the High Court challenge.

Speakers at the protest included Dr Shamikh Badra, who is from Gaza. He called on the federal government to act for Palestine, and not allow the weapons trade to continue.

Badra condemned the strike on Nasser Hospital in southern Gaza. He said people were still being denied food, medical assistance and other aid, and recent floods had made their lives even more unbearable.

Sue Higginson, NSW Greens MLC, called on Labor to help. “The genocidal state of Israel will not let in the support. There are people [who have been] flooded, People have lost the only shelter they had — which was a flipping tent for goodness sake. And they can’t replace it.” She said Australia needs to impose a boycott, sanctions and divestment regime on Israel.

Meanwhile, foreign minister Penny Wong announced on November 16, that Australia had signed a joint statement with Canada, Italy and Britain urging Israel to allow “immediate, rapid and unimpeded humanitarian access throughout Gaza ... before it is too late.”

Brian Mahony reports that protesters gathered in Gumbaynggirr Country/Coffs Harbour to join the November 15 national day of action to defend free speech and the right to protest.

Protesters also called for an end to Australia’s ongoing arms trade with Israel.

Cas Smith reports that about 300 people gathered at Russell Square in Boorloo/Perth on November 15 to call for an end to Israel's genocide in Gaza.

Speakers included Sarah Pickles from Right to Protest WA, primary school student Sakeenah Azizi, Palestinian-Australian Dareen Allagta, Sam Wainwright from the WA Anti-War Collective and Neda Blackwood from Teachers for Palestine WA.

The crowd were moved to tears by a performance from musical duo the Paddystinians — Johny Bravo and Ozzie Hishmeh.

A Paddle out for Palestine was held in Muloobinba/Newcastle on November 14, as part of Rising Tide’s Paddle for the Planet at Horseshoe Beach. Rachel Evans from City of Sydney for Palestine reminded the crowd that war and occupation is a climate issue.

NSW Greens MLC Sue Higginson said climate and Palestine protests are both being targeted by the Minns government’s undemocratic anti-protest laws. She said Newcastle City Council’s ban on Rising Tide events on council land would also apply to Palestine solidarity rallies.

Liberal National Party of Queensland (LNP)

2023–26 Israeli genocide on Gaza

author: Suzanne James
title: Calvary takeover raises questions over hospital licences and access to VAD
content:
The proposed takeover of 14 former Healthscope hospitals by Catholic healthcare provider Calvary Health Care is facing scrutiny over competition, corporate accountability and the future availability of lawful healthcare services, including voluntary assisted dying (VAD).

Calvary’s proposed acquisition includes six NSW hospitals: Newcastle Private, Hunter Valley Private, Norwest, Lady Davidson, The Hills Private and The Sydney Clinic.

Calvary has confirmed it will not offer or facilitate VAD in any acquired hospital. Other excluded services under its Catholic healthcare guidelines include in vitro fertilisation (IVF) and assisted reproductive technologies, elective terminations, vasectomies, tubal ligation and gender care procedures.

The implications are particularly significant in the Hunter. Newcastle Private has an established role in providing VAD services. Go Gentle Australia reports that the hospital is understood to receive approximately one or two VAD requests each week.

Calvary says patients requesting VAD will continue to receive compassionate care and that appropriate pathways will be explored. However, transferring seriously ill patients elsewhere can create considerable practical, clinical and personal difficulties, particularly near the end of life.

The proposed takeover prompted a powerful protest on November 8, with hundreds calling on NSW Labor to protect access to existing healthcare services.

Dying With Dignity NSW supporters and Board members joined community members and healthcare professionals in raising concerns about the loss of established services.

Two regulatory approvals are required for the takeover to proceed. The NSW government is expected to determine the transfer of the six hospital licences on December 1.

Under section 15(4)(a) of the NSW Private Health Facilities Act 2007, the health secretary can consider whether the applicant is a fit and proper person to hold a hospital licence. This assessment can consider the corporate applicant itself, as well as its directors and relevant management personnel.

This raises the question of whether governance, oversight and organisational accountability findings arising from the Mater Hospital inquiry could be relevant to Calvary’s suitability. Any such findings would need to be attributable to the relevant Calvary entity; responsibility cannot simply be assumed.

Separately, the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission is examining the acquisition’s implications for hospital market competition. Its assessment timetable has recently been extended to December 10.

These decisions will have consequences beyond hospital ownership, potentially affecting the availability of established healthcare services and patients’ access to lawful choices, including VAD.

[Suzanne James is an advocate for voluntary assisted dying.]

author: Jim McIlroy
title: Union slams Qantas’ plan to outsource 850 jobs
content:
The Australian Services Union (ASU) has slammed Qantas’ plan to outsource about 850 head office jobs to tech services firm Accenture.

Qantas said that it will cut hundreds of local jobs on November 10 after making a deal with Accenture to “modernise its back-end systems, processes and data”. It will mean that the airline’s back office functions will “mostly” be shifted to India, according to the Sydney Morning Herald on November 11.

The first phase of the job cuts and outsourcing will affect staff in finance, procurement, human resources and marketing.

The ASU on November 11 demanded Qantas “keep its commitment” to employees when it told them in August that it had “no plan to offshore any Australian jobs”. It said workers “deserved an honest explanation” of what had changed.

The union is demanding Qantas provide details about how many roles and which will be cut, as well as how many will remain in Australia.

It also wants a retraining plan for experienced staff to be able to move to other roles in the company, good redundancy packages for those whose jobs will go, and consultation the ASU before individual’s outcomes are decided.

ASU assistant national secretary Scott Cowen said Qantas has a bad history of outsourcing and offshoring jobs.

“AI is having a huge impact on workers,” Cowen said, “but the cost of technology change should not be borne by the workers who have kept the airline running for years.”

Cowen asked if AI is being used as cover for Qantas’ plans to offshore jobs. “Is this using AI as the excuse to say the work can’t be done internally because it’s new or too specialised?”

Angus McFarland, ASU NSW & ACT secretary, said the job cuts are more evidence that Qantas’ culture has not changed under new leadership. “CEO Vanessa Hudson promised Australians a different Qantas. Instead she’s reaching straight for [former airline CEO] Alan Joyce’s old blueprint.” He said there is “nothing innovative” about shipping Australian jobs overseas to cut costs.

The ASU criticised Qantas’ communication to its employees where it confirmed that work will move predominantly to India. The airline confirmed that there will be no new AI systems or AI agents.

McFarland said: “Technology should be used to make jobs better, not to provide another excuse to get rid of the people doing the hard work.” He recalled how Qantas had illegally outsourced 1700 ground-handling workers under CEO Alan Joyce. “We were told Vanessa Hudson would lead a new chapter, but here we are again.”

The ASU said Qantas’ claims about investing in Australian jobs elsewhere in the business does not justify the cuts.

The union is demanding that Qantas abandon the proposed outsourcing and guarantee that no employee will be forced out as a result of the Accenture deal. It said it will fight to protect every job affected by the proposal.

“There is still time to stop Qantas’ plans. They’ve confirmed that no final decisions have been made about individual roles,” McFarland said.

Despite the slowing world economy, Qantas reported almost $1.3 billion in full-year profits in August.

The roots of the Qantas crisis go back to the Paul Keating Labor government’s decision to privatise Australia’s major publicly-owned airline in the early 1990s.

The union movement should launch a major drive to take the airline back into public hands, under workers’ control. It could be the first step in the development of an integrated public transport system, linked to a massive expansion of the national railway network and reduce carbon pollution in a climate-challenged world.

[Jim McIlroy is a life-long public sector unionist.]

Australian Services Union (ASU)

author: Daniel Avalos
title: La justicia solo muerde los pies de los descalzos
content:
Un pedazo de carne, 36 días presa y una pregunta sobre la Justicia.

 Fotos y texto Daniel Ávalos para Anred.




Estela Chávez: 36 días detenida por un pedazo de carne, tiene más de 65 años, cobra la jubilación mínima y estuvo 36 días privada de su libertad por un presunto intento de hurto en un supermercado. Su familia reunió los $150.000 de caución para que recuperara la libertad. La causa sigue abierta. Su historia excede un episodio policial y abre una discusión sobre la Justicia, la pobreza y el papel del Estado en un contexto donde la respuesta represiva gana terreno. Estela trabajó durante años limpiando casas. Como tantas mujeres, pasó buena parte de su vida ocupándose de los hogares de otros. Tuvo seis hijos y, cuando ya no pudo seguir trabajando, accedió a la jubilación a través de una moratoria previsional. Hoy cobra el haber mínimo y vive en un barrio popular de San Fernando junto a una de sus nietas.El 8 de octubre fue detenida en un supermercado.




La acusación: intentar llevarse un corte de carne sin pagar. La interceptaron antes de cruzar la línea de cajas. Ese episodio terminó con Estela en una alcaidía, donde permaneció durante 36 días.El 26 de octubre se dictó su prisión preventiva. Fue alojada en la Alcaidía N.º 15, en Chacarita. Compartió una celda con otras cinco mujeres, tuvo una intoxicación con la comida y debió ser trasladada a un hospital. La familia podía acercarle ropa y elementos de higiene, pero no tenía permitido visitarla.Recién el 13 de noviembre recuperó la libertad. Para conseguirlo, sus familiares tuvieron que reunir los $150.000 fijados como caución. La causa por tentativa de hurto continúa abierta.Hay algo difícil de pasar por alto: una mujer que trabajó durante décadas, que cobra una jubilación mínima y que vive con ingresos insuficientes terminó privada de su libertad por un hecho vinculado con alimentos. ¿Era necesario mantenerla detenida durante 36 días? ¿Qué riesgos procesales justificaban esa decisión? ¿Qué otras alternativas podían haberse considerado?La prisión preventiva no es una condena. Es una medida excepcional que debe tener fundamentos concretos. En el caso de Estela no contamos con la resolución judicial completa ni conocemos en detalle los argumentos que llevaron a dictarla y sostenerla durante más de un mes. Pero esa falta de información tampoco clausura las preguntas sobre la proporcionalidad de la medida y sobre el trato que reciben las personas en situaciones de vulnerabilidad. Cuando la Justicia también forma parte del problema,la actuación judicial no puede analizarse como si ocurriera al margen de la sociedad en la que interviene. Tampoco alcanza con pensarla como una institución que simplemente aplica leyes. Sus decisiones tienen consecuencias concretas: determinan quién queda detenido, quién recupera la libertad y quién tiene que esperar detrás de una reja mientras se investiga una acusación.En la provincia de Buenos Aires, la Comisión Provincial por la Memoria viene advirtiendo sobre el funcionamiento de una cadena punitiva que articula a las fuerzas de seguridad, la Justicia penal y el sistema penitenciario. En su informe anual de 2026 señala que las prácticas policiales violentas encuentran con frecuencia una respuesta judicial que las convalida, en lugar de controlarlas.




Los números también hablan. Durante 2025 se dictaron 20.995 prisiones preventivas en la provincia, el 47% de las privaciones de libertad ordenadas ese año. Según el mismo informe, las personas detenidas pasaron, en promedio, 412 días privadas de su libertad hasta la sentencia de primera instancia. Todavía eran legalmente inocentes durante ese período.No son datos menores. Muestran hasta qué punto el encierro previo a una condena se ha extendido dentro del sistema penal. En estos tiempos, además, la discusión sobre la Justicia no puede separarse del avance de las políticas represivas. Mientras se endurece el discurso sobre la seguridad, se estigmatiza la protesta social y se multiplican las intervenciones de las fuerzas de seguridad frente a quienes reclaman, también crece la preocupación por el papel de las instituciones que deberían controlar esos procedimientos. La Comisión Interamericana de Derechos Humanos expresó su preocupación por las restricciones al derecho a la protesta en Argentina, la violencia estatal en las movilizaciones y el uso de mecanismos judiciales que pueden limitar el debate público.¿Dónde queda la independencia judicial cuando las garantías parecen perder terreno frente a las políticas de orden y disciplinamiento? ¿Qué distancia conserva la Justicia respecto de los discursos y las decisiones del poder político? Son preguntas que no se responden con un solo expediente, pero que tampoco pueden seguir esquivándose. No se trata de afirmar que todos los jueces actúan de la misma manera ni de desconocer la complejidad de cada causa. Se trata de mirar qué prácticas se repiten, a quiénes alcanzan y qué controles existen sobre el poder de detener y encarcelar. Una Justicia que no revisa el accionar policial, que naturaliza la prisión preventiva y que reserva las alternativas al encierro para unos pocos corre el riesgo de convertirse en una pieza más del dispositivo represivo. La persecución penal recae con mucha más facilidad sobre quienes tienen menos recursos para defenderse. La pobreza aparece entonces bajo una doble forma: primero como falta de acceso a derechos básicos y después como una condición que deja a las personas más expuestas frente al sistema penal.




La historia de Estela no empieza en la puerta de un supermercado. Viene de mucho antes. De una vida de trabajo y de mujeres que hicieron tareas domésticas durante años, pero llegaron a la vejez sin una protección económica suficiente.




Los números ayudan a entenderlo. En noviembre de 2026, la jubilación mínima es de $444.158,46. Con el bono extraordinario de $70.000 llega a $514.158,46. El último dato del INDEC ubicó en $546.926 la canasta básica total para un adulto equivalente, el ingreso de referencia para no quedar bajo la línea de pobreza. Incluso con el bono, la jubilación mínima queda por debajo de ese valor. La diferencia supera los $32.000. Y hablamos de una referencia general, que no contempla necesariamente los gastos particulares que puede tener una persona mayor: medicamentos, tratamientos, consultas médicas o cuidados. La carne también tiene sus propios números. En octubre, el INDEC registró un kilo de carne picada común a $10.778,88 y uno de asado a $16.957,55 en los precios relevados para el Gran Buenos Aires. Para quien vive de una jubilación mínima, cada compra exige hacer cuentas y dejar algo afuera.No hace falta exagerar. Basta con mirar los ingresos y el precio de los alimentos.Pero hay otra cuestión: cuando la necesidad aparece en un expediente penal, ¿qué lugar ocupa la historia de esa persona? ¿La Justicia mira solamente el hecho que se investiga o también considera las condiciones en las que vive quien tiene delante? No se trata de desconocer las leyes ni de sostener que la situación económica justifica cualquier conducta. Se trata de discutir cómo se aplica la ley y si la respuesta del Estado guarda proporción con los hechos. La igualdad ante la Justicia no debería depender de cuánto dinero tiene una persona para defenderse, de sus posibilidades de reunir una caución o de contar con alguien que pueda asistirla. Mientras el ajuste deteriora las condiciones de vida de amplios sectores de la población, quienes quedan más expuestos deben enfrentar también las consecuencias de ese deterioro. Primero aparece la dificultad para llegar a fin de mes. Después, la imposibilidad de cubrir necesidades básicas. Y, en determinadas circunstancias, una situación de necesidad puede terminar convertida en un expediente policial. Estela recuperó la libertad, pero su situación cotidiana no cambió. Sigue teniendo que vivir con una jubilación que no alcanza y todavía tiene una causa abierta. El estado la criminalizó, no se va preocupar de como seguirá su vida, si tendrá que salir otra vez a robar para comer, ella salió y lo primero que hizo fue emocionarse y creo que fue porque vió que había un mínimo de la sociedad que sabia que existia. La pregunta, entonces, no es solamente qué pasó en aquel supermercado. También es qué sociedad permite que una mujer que trabajó toda su vida llegue a la vejez sin poder garantizarse algo tan básico como la comida. Y qué Justicia construimos cuando el peso de la ley parece sentirse con mayor fuerza sobre quienes menos tienen.




Que harías si no tenes para comer y nada ni nadie te da una respuesta?

author: CMI Argentina
title: Mendoza: docentes se reunieron para tratar los problemas de la educación rural
content:
En Mendoza se conformó un espacio de encuentro entre educadores y educadoras huarpes de distintas comunidades rurales. La propuesta busca compartir experiencias, poner en debate las prácticas escolares y fortalecer el reconocimiento de la identidad y los saberes del pueblo Huarpe en las escuelas.










Escuchar el reporte de Radio Tierra Campesina de Mendoza




En el primer encuentro realizado en la comunidad del Cavadito participaron alrededor de ocho docentes que se desempeñan en distintas localidades del secano, entre ellas El Cavadito, San Miguel, El Forzudo, San José y Lagunas del Rosario. La mayoría trabaja en el nivel primario, aunque también hay educadores del secundario.




La propuesta comenzó a tomar forma a partir del vínculo entre docentes del territorio y un equipo de extensión universitaria integrado por Carla Rosales y Mercedes Molina.




En diálogo con Radio Tierra Campesina, Molina explicó: “La idea es pensar a la educación como un derecho, entonces la posibilidad de terminar la escuela secundaria tiene que ser una posibilidad real para los chicos y chicas que están ahí”.




También se abordan las dificultades que atraviesa la educación rural y la importancia de que las políticas educativas tengan en cuenta las particularidades de cada territorio. “Plantear lo que significa la identidad huarpe para los docentes, para el equipo de directivos, estas tensiones frente a las identidades y al reconocimiento, si está validado o no, qué implicancias tiene esto con las decisiones dentro de la escuela”, relató Carla Rosales.




Los educadores buscan fortalecer sus vínculos y seguir construyendo herramientas colectivas para defender una educación pública que reconozca los saberes y la identidad de los pueblos.




“La educación rural en este contexto se lleva la peor parte, para la economía dos más dos son cuatro y si hay poca gente sacas esa cuenta y parece que en la ruralidad eso no cierra”, concluyó Rosales.
